status: implemented optional ablation; CPU numerical and gradient fixture passed; performance unmeasured
name: Training-only two-view identity-projection NT-Xent regularizer
interface: contrastive_regularizer(model, kind, batch_db, device, temperature=0.2, seed=0, source_groups=None) -> scalar Tensor

input.missingness: NaN only; each window must contain at least one observed cell; infinities rejected
input.encoder_input: pipeline.mixtures.cnn_channels(view)[0], float32 N x 4 x 15 x 25
input.representation: model.representation(x), pooled hidden features with gradients connected
input.source_boundary: Caller must supply training-source examples only. Function reads no dataset, model file, population statistics or target.

view_design.transformation: Independent per-window scalar gains, uniform [-3,+3] dB, one for each of two views
view_design.target_invariance: If the same g>0 multiplies both background B and added component R under the same mask O, sum(O*g*R)/sum(O*g*(B+R)) equals the original fraction exactly.
view_design.changed: Absolute dB channel only, apart from floating-point roundoff; stochastic encoder dropout provides another source of view variation.
view_design.reason_for_exclusions: These operations can remove/reweight component energy or change the observed-mask target, so retaining the original target would be unjustified without known-component recomputation.

loss.construction: Concatenate the 2N hidden representations, L2 normalize, compute cosine similarity / temperature, exclude self similarities, retain counterpart view as the positive, and apply cross_entropy averaged over both view directions.
loss.projection: Identity. No trainable head is created dynamically and no extra parameters can be omitted from an already-created optimizer.
loss.simclr_difference: SimCLR uses a learned nonlinear projection head and its own image augmentations. This implementation borrows the NT-Xent form and two-view structure only; it is not a SimCLR reproduction or an underwater SOTA claim.
loss.combined_objective: Existing supervised energy-fraction MSE + existing auxiliary losses + lambda * NT-Xent; lambda defaults to zero.
loss.temperature_status: Starting ablation value, not a validated optimum
loss.no_negative_policy: Return a gradient-connected scalar zero when fewer than two unique instances remain or no eligible negative is available.

false_negative_controls.batch_duplicates: Keep one input per observed mask and canonical relative dB grid rounded to 1 mdB. This avoids many identical/common-gain copies as false negatives, but quantization boundaries can miss floating-point-near equivalents.
false_negative_controls.optional_source_groups: When nonmissing group IDs are provided, same-group candidates are removed from the negative set. Their paired views remain positive.
false_negative_controls.current_caller_limitation: The agreed training caller passes batch_db without source_groups. Repeated reference/background sources and semantically related windows can therefore remain false negatives.
false_negative_controls.remaining_risk: Different source groups are not certified different semantic classes. Source masking does not implement the Debiased Contrastive Learning estimator or remove every false negative.
false_negative_controls.future_gate: Carry frozen training recipe source IDs into a group-aware sampler or mask, check effective unique negative counts, and compare with the zero-weight baseline using locked validation only.

reproducibility.numpy_rng: Local Generator, caller NumPy RNG unchanged
reproducibility.torch_rng: fork_rng restores CPU and target CUDA streams; a local CPU generator and target-device CUDA seed supply stochastic encoder views
reproducibility.seed_policy: Caller changes seed per training epoch and batch and records it; fixed seed reproduces the CPU fixture.
reproducibility.state: Input batch is not modified, no parameters are created, and eval-mode use is rejected.

tests: Known-component fraction invariant under common gain
Missing mask and original inputs preserved
Relative/energy-weight channels invariant within numerical tolerance
All three real encoder implementations return finite loss with finite nonzero gradients
CPU RNG restored and repeated seed produces equal loss
Duplicate-only, singleton and same-group-only batches return differentiable zero
Unsupported kind, eval mode, all-missing input, infinity and invalid temperature rejected
verification.result_meaning: These values establish interface/autograd/numerical behavior only. They do not measure learning progress, competition RMSE or generalization.

selection_policy.enabled_experiment: Use a new run tag and freeze baseline/ablation seeds, data version and training budget. Evaluate supervised RMSE on existing locked validation; preserve identical preprocessing and ensemble procedures.
do_not_use: Calibration for contrastive fitting or ablation selection
selection_policy.adoption: Only a reproducible supervised validation improvement can justify enabling this regularizer. Do not use decreasing contrastive loss alone as evidence.

limitations: Only common gain changes the input, so augmentation diversity is deliberately weak and may add little useful supervision.
Instance discrimination can encode source or sensor signatures and push similar vessel/background events apart.
Identity projection directly constrains features needed by the regression objective; auxiliary gradients may conflict with supervised MSE.
The original SimCLR evidence is from image classification and SimCSE evidence is from sentence embeddings, not this energy-share task.
A small source pool cannot be made independent by increasing synthetic combinations or contrastive batch size.
The 2N x 2N similarity matrix uses quadratic batch memory, and two extra encoder views increase compute; batch size must be benchmarked on the rented GPU.
CUDA numerical behavior, actual training stability, effective group-aware negatives and performance remain unmeasured.

primary_sources.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
primary_sources.verified_claim: Two stochastic views, cosine normalization, temperature-scaled cross entropy, projection-head and batch-size effects. These establish the borrowed method components, not superiority on this competition.

primary_sources.title: Debiased Contrastive Learning
primary_sources.authors: Chuang, Robinson, Lin, Torralba and Jegelka
primary_sources.verified_claim: Random negatives can share the semantic label and bias learning. Its proposed debiasing estimator is not implemented here.

primary_sources.title: SimCSE: Simple Contrastive Learning of Sentence Embeddings
primary_sources.verified_claim: Dropout can form positive views without input deletion in sentence representation learning. Applying this idea to an energy grid is an unvalidated inference.

primary_sources.title: PyTorch functional.normalize
primary_sources.verified_claim: Differentiable L2 normalization with an epsilon floor; no out= tensor is used.

primary_sources.title: PyTorch functional.cross_entropy
primary_sources.verified_claim: Cross entropy accepts unnormalized logits and integer class targets.

primary_sources.title: PyTorch random and CUDA seeding
primary_sources.verified_claim: RNG forking/state restoration and explicit generators support isolated reproducible views; CUDA manual_seed applies to the current GPU.
